pages.title: Self-Healing Polymer
pages.text: A rubbery strip that, cut cleanly in two, slowly finds itself again. Its chains carry reversible bonds that break and reform, so pressing the halves together lets them rebond across the seam. It is warm and a little sticky at the cut.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I wanted a material that repaired itself the way skin does. Nanotube rope gave it strength, slime gave it reversible bonds, and a topological circuit board gave the bonds a pattern to restore. The first sample healed overnight.
Made in $(item)Chemical Reactor$() and $(item)Knot Loom$().$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): Supramolecular Chemistry.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Minimal Synthetic Cell.
